title: Trapped between two limits
objectives: Write two conditions as one double inequality
Solve a double inequality by acting on all three parts
List and count the whole numbers that satisfy it

screens.prose: A number now has to pass two tests at once: $x > -2$ and $x \le 3$. Each test is drawn as a bar.
screens.question: Tap every whole number that passes both tests.

hints.text: A dot must sit under both bars.
Check the two ends: −2 and 3.
−2 fails the first test, since −2 is not bigger than −2. 3 passes the second, since 3 is at most 3.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep a dot only if it passes both tests.

byKey.took-low: You tapped −2. It fails the first test: −2 is not bigger than −2.
byKey.dropped-three: You left out 3. The second test is $x \le 3$, and 3 is equal to 3, so it passes.
byKey.one-test: You checked only the first test. 4 and 5 fail $x \le 3$.
byKey.m2: You tapped −2. It fails the first test: −2 is not bigger than −2.
byKey.n4: 4 passes the first test but fails $x \le 3$.

explain.text: The bars overlap from just after −2 up to 3. Five whole numbers sit in that overlap. −2 is out, at a hollow end; 3 is in, at a filled end.

explain.text: The overlap runs from −2, left out, to 3, kept in. It is one bar with an end on each side. Every number in it passes both tests.

screens.prose: We write the overlap as one **double inequality**: $x$ sits between two limits, with the smaller limit on the left.
screens.question: Which double inequality matches the bar?

options.why: You swapped the ends. The dot at −2 is hollow, so −2 is out; the dot at 3 is filled, so 3 is in.
That leaves 3 out. The dot at 3 is filled, so 3 belongs.
Each symbol must point the same way. Read from left to right, smallest first: $-2 < x \le 3$.

hints.text: Read each end: hollow or filled?
The left end is hollow; the right end is filled.
Hollow at −2 gives $-2 < x$. Filled at 3 gives $x \le 3$. Join them: $-2 < x \le 3$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read each end separately, then join them.

explain.text: $-2 < x \le 3$ packs both tests into one line. Read it as “$x$ is bigger than −2 and at most 3”. Each symbol matches the dot at its end.

screens.prose: Solve $1 < 2x + 3 \le 11$. A double inequality has three parts. Whatever you do, do it to all three.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

screens.question: Tap moves until $x$ is alone in the middle.

ops.label: Subtract 3 from the middle only
ops.why: You took 3 from the middle but not from the ends. That changes the limits. Do the same to all three parts.

ops.label: Divide all three parts by 2 and reverse the signs
ops.why: You reversed the signs, but 2 is positive. Only a negative divisor flips them.

hints.text: What is done to $x$ last? Undo it in all three parts.
Take 3 from the left, the middle and the right.
Subtract 3 everywhere to get $-2 < 2x \le 8$. Then divide everywhere by 2.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each move must reach all three parts.

byKey.s0w: You took 3 from the middle only. The 1 and the 11 must lose 3 as well.
byKey.s1w: You reversed the signs after dividing by 2. A positive divisor keeps them.

explain.text: You subtracted 3 from all three parts, then divided all three by 2. Both moves keep the signs. The solution is a bar from −1, left out, to 4, kept in.

screens.prose: The solution was $-1 < x \le 4$. Often only whole numbers make sense, such as a number of shares.
screens.question: How many whole numbers satisfy $-1 < x \le 4$?

hints.text: Is −1 in? Is 4 in?
The left dot is hollow and the right dot is filled.
−1 is out and 4 is in. List them: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. List the whole numbers on the bar, checking each end.

byKey.both-ends: You counted −1. The hollow end leaves −1 out.
byKey.no-ends: You left out 4. The filled end keeps 4 in.
byKey.subtract: You worked out 4 − 1. The lower limit is −1, so the gap is 4 − (−1) = 5.

explain.text: The bar holds 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. −1 sits at the hollow end, so it is out. 4 sits at the filled end, so it is in.

screens.prose: Solve $-3 \le 1 - 2x < 7$. Subtracting 1 from all three parts gives $-4 \le -2x < 6$.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

screens.question: Finish the solution. Tap moves until $x$ is alone, smallest limit on the left.

ops.label: Divide all three parts by $-2$
ops.why: You kept both signs after dividing by $-2$. That says $x \ge 2$ and $x < -3$ at once, which no number does.

ops.label: Divide all three parts by $-2$ and reverse the first sign
ops.why: Dividing by $-2$ reverses every comparison, so both signs turn round.

ops.label: Divide all three parts by $-2$ and reverse both signs
Rewrite with the smallest limit on the left

hints.text: What does dividing by $-2$ do to the order of numbers?
Both comparisons are affected, not just one.
Divide by $-2$ and turn both signs: $2 \ge x > -3$. Then read it from the smaller end.

feedback.correct: $-3 < x \le 2$. Check $x = 0$: $1 - 0 = 1$, which is between −3 and 7.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Dividing by $-2$ reverses both signs.

byKey.w1: You kept both signs after dividing by $-2$. That says $x \ge 2$ and $x < -3$ at once, which no number does.
byKey.w2: You reversed only one sign. Dividing by a negative turns every comparison round, so both signs flip.

explain.text: Dividing by $-2$ mirrors all three parts, so both signs reverse: $2 \ge x > -3$. Read from the smaller end, that is $-3 < x \le 2$. A result that no number satisfies, like $2 \le x < -3$, is a sign you missed a flip.

screens.prose: The rules you used: $$a < x \le b \quad\text{means}\quad x > a \text{ and } x \le b$$ Do the same thing to all three parts. Dividing by a negative reverses both signs. Then count whole numbers from the ends.
screens.question: For whole numbers $a < b$, how many whole numbers satisfy $a < x \le b$?

options.why: That counts both ends. But $a$ is left out by the hollow end.
That leaves out both ends. But $b$ is kept in by the filled end.

feedback.correct: $b - a$. Check: $4 - (-1) = 5$, the count you found.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Test your choice on $-1 < x \le 4$, which has 5 whole numbers.

explain.text: From $a + 1$ up to $b$ there are $b - a$ whole numbers. For $-1 < x \le 4$ that is $4 - (-1) = 5$. With both ends filled, add 1; with both hollow, subtract 1.

screens.prose: A market maker must keep her position $q$ within $-200 \le q \le 200$ shares. She is long 120 now. Selling $n$ shares leaves $120 - n$, so $$-200 \le 120 - n \le 200$$
screens.question: What is the most shares she can sell?

hints.text: Selling moves her position left on the line. How far can it go?
The lowest position allowed is −200. She starts at 120.
Subtract 120 throughout: $-320 \le -n \le 80$. Multiply by $-1$ and reverse: $-80 \le n \le 320$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find how far she can move left from 120 before reaching −200.

byKey.to-zero: You stopped at a flat position. She may go short, down to −200.
byKey.limit-only: You used the limit alone. Starting long 120, she sells 120 to reach 0, then 200 more.
byKey.flipped: 80 is the most she can buy. Buying is a negative sale, the other end of $-80 \le n \le 320$.

explain.text: Subtracting 120 gives $-320 \le -n \le 80$, and multiplying by $-1$ reverses both signs: $-80 \le n \le 320$. She can sell up to 320 shares or buy up to 80. On the line that is the walk from 120 down to −200.

screens.prose: Your account holds £5,000.00. Each futures contract ties up £450.00 of margin. You must keep at least £800.00 free. With $n$ contracts: $$5000 - 450n \ge 800$$
screens.question: What is the largest number of contracts you can hold?

hints.text: Get the $n$ term alone first: subtract 5000 from both sides.
You reach $-450n \ge -4200$. Divide by $-450$, and mind the sign.
$n \le 4200 \div 450 = 9.33$. You cannot hold part of a contract.

feedback.correct: 9 contracts leave £950.00 free. 10 would leave only £500.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Solve for $n$, then take the largest whole number allowed.

byKey.not-whole: Contracts come whole. 9.33 is the limit, so the most you can hold is 9.
byKey.no-buffer: You split the whole £5,000.00 into contracts. £800.00 must stay free.
byKey.added-buffer: You added the £800.00 to the account. It must be kept back, so subtract it.
byKey.rounded-up: 10 contracts use £4,500.00 and leave £500.00, below the £800.00 floor. Round down.

explain.text: $5000 - 450n \ge 800$ gives $-450n \ge -4200$. Dividing by $-450$ reverses the sign: $n \le 9.33$. The largest whole number allowed is 9, which leaves £950.00 free.

ideas: Two tests at once give a bar between two limits: $a < x \le b$ means $x > a$ and $x \le b$.
Solve by doing the same thing to all three parts. Dividing by a negative reverses both signs.
Count whole numbers from the ends: $a < x \le b$ holds $b - a$ of them, one end in and one out.

formula.name: Double inequality
formula.tex: a < x \le b \iff x > a \text{ and } x \le b
formula.note: The smaller limit goes on the left, and both symbols point the same way.
